decisions.decision: Version input data for reproducible forecasts
decisions.context: Past weekly forecasts must be reproducible. The design space offers repository based data versioning and alternatives without data versioning (d:11).

alternatives.label: No data versioning
cons: Reproducibility: past inputs may be unavailable

decisions.rationale: Reproducing a past week is the deciding driver, so retain explicit data versions despite the added workflow. The design point combining this with model quality testing, rollback, and scheduled runs returned no warnings, but no attesting sources.
consequences: Record the data version used for each forecast run.
Maintain storage and retrieval for historical data versions.

decisions.decision: What to test before accepting a model
decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production quickly without breaking the weekly run. The design space includes model quality tests and no testing (d:26).

alternatives.label: Testing trained model quality
pros: Protect weekly run: checks model quality

alternatives.label: Unit testing feature engineering logic
pros: Protect weekly run: catches feature logic errors

alternatives.label: No testing
cons: Protect weekly run: regressions may pass unnoticed

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: evaluate candidate model quality before release, accepting added evaluation work. The design point returned no warnings, while the rival combination with no testing did too; neither point had attesting sources.
consequences: Define quality checks for candidate forecasts before release.
Account for evaluation time in the model delivery workflow.

decisions.decision: How to roll out and recover a model
decisions.context: A new model must reach production without disrupting the weekly forecast. The design space considers rollback, multiple production versions, and a single production model (d:10).

alternatives.label: Rollback to previous model version
cons: Production speed: rollback needs a release step

alternatives.label: N versions in production
cons: Protect weekly run: increases operational complexity

alternatives.label: Single model in production
pros: Protect weekly run: simpler production state
cons: Production speed: less room for gradual rollout

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: make recovery to a known model version part of deployment, at the cost of a rollback step. The design point returned no warnings; its rival using a single production model also returned no warnings, and neither had attesting sources.
consequences: Keep the previous model version available for recovery.
Include rollback in the release procedure.

decisions.decision: How to trigger the forecast pipeline
decisions.context: Demand is forecast weekly, and changes should not break that run. The design space includes scheduled and commit triggered pipeline runs (d:12).

alternatives.label: On-schedule trigger
pros: Protect weekly run: supports weekly cadence
cons: Production speed: experiments may await schedule

alternatives.label: On-commit trigger
pros: Production speed: starts work after changes
cons: Protect weekly run: changes may trigger unintended runs

alternatives.label: On-demand trigger
pros: Protect weekly run: run timing is controlled

decisions.rationale: Protecting the weekly run decides the choice: schedule the production forecast to its required cadence, accepting that experiments may not run immediately. The chosen design point returned no warnings; its on-commit rival also returned no warnings, and neither had attesting sources.
consequences: Set and maintain the weekly production schedule.
Provide a separate controlled path for ad hoc experiments.

decisions.context: A three person team owns the pipeline end to end and wants new ideas to reach production quickly. The design space includes CI/CD pipelines and manually run build and deployment scripts (d:8).

alternatives.label: CI/CD pipeline
pros: Production speed: automates delivery on changes
cons: Protect weekly run: requires safe release checks

alternatives.label: Build and Deployment scripts
pros: Protect weekly run: deployment can be explicitly initiated

alternatives.label: No integration or delivery automation
pros: Protect weekly run: avoids automatic releases

decisions.rationale: Production speed decides the choice: automate integration and delivery, accepting the need for release checks to protect the weekly run. This is grounded in the design space alternatives (d:8), but was not included in the checked design points.
consequences: Maintain automated integration and delivery workflows.
Gate production releases on the selected model quality checks.

decisions.decision: Process weekly demand data in batches
decisions.context: The system forecasts weekly demand per store and product. The design space contrasts batch and real time processing (d:15).

alternatives.label: Batch-based data processing
pros: Protect weekly run: fits scheduled processing
cons: Protect weekly run: depends on batch completion timing

alternatives.label: Real-time, stream-based data processing
pros: Protect weekly run: supports continuously arriving data
cons: Protect weekly run: adds stream processing complexity

decisions.rationale: The weekly forecast cadence decides the choice: batch processing matches the stated workload without requiring continuous processing. This is grounded in the design space alternatives (d:15), but was not included in the checked design points.
consequences: Coordinate data availability with the weekly forecast schedule.
Monitor batch completion before publishing forecasts.
